title: Conegums
summary: Conegums is a Mattituck creek name recorded by Tooker. He identifies the stream with Reeve's Creek, later known as James Creek, near the boundary between Southold and Riverhead.
map_geometry_source: Imported polygon retained. Conegums is identified with Reeve's Creek, later James Creek, near the Southold-Riverhead boundary and the Mattituck Bay canoe-drag route.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Corchaug Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Conegums preserves a Mattituck creek name interpreted as a boundary, identified with Reeve's Creek and later James Creek near the Southold-Riverhead line. As a named bound, the creek shows how waterways could organize land agreements, movement, and memory across the North Fork. Creeks were not minor features; they could mark limits, guide travel, and carry Native geography into later maps and town records.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted Conegums as meaning a boundary because the creek served as the east bound of the tract. Related modern names include Reeve's Creek and James Creek; Tooker also points readers to Kanungum for comparison.

Why Place Names Matter

“Families who lived and hunted on the Land applied names to help them remember where the currents, the caribou crossings, the seagull nesting sites and a myriad of other landmarks were located.”

— Lynn Peplinski, Place Names (2018), Article paragraph 3
land_loss_content: Conegums shows how Indigenous geographic knowledge shaped colonial land descriptions. A creek, a canoe route, and a bay connection remained central reference points as Native land was converted into deeded property.
whereintheworld_content: The existing polygon marks the James Creek/Reeve's Creek area at Mattituck. It represents a general creek landscape and boundary area, not a surveyed reconstruction of the 1648 tract.
